skill.name: deepseek-vision-bridge
skill.description: Deploy a local bridge that adds OCR, cloud or local image understanding, and image generation workflows to text-only DeepSeek clients.
skill.summary: Connect text-only DeepSeek clients to OCR, vision models, and image generation through a configurable local proxy.
skill.author: lightlw

security_audit.summary: Many static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, templates, loopback addresses, and JavaScript template literals. Confirmed risks include shell injection, credential-bearing network forwarding, sensitive configuration access, unauthenticated all-interface listening, SSRF, and Windows autostart persistence. The generated tool output also contains an instruction that discourages image verification.

remediation.issue: Shell commands include CLI-controlled prompt and path values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace exec and shell-enabled execSync with spawn or execFile argument arrays. Validate filenames, output paths, scheduler names, and model options.

remediation.issue: The credential-bearing proxy accepts unauthenticated connections on all interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Bind explicitly to 127.0.0.1, require a separate client token, restrict methods and paths, and enforce request size limits.

remediation.issue: Inbound image URLs can access arbitrary network destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only approved HTTPS hosts. Resolve addresses before requests, block private and metadata ranges, limit redirects, timeouts, and response sizes.

remediation.issue: Tool output instructs the agent not to inspect generated images.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the REMINDER directive. Return a neutral output path and allow the calling agent to apply its normal verification policy.

remediation.issue: The Windows installer creates hidden autostart persistence with policy bypass.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation, avoid hidden windows and ExecutionPolicy Bypass, show the exact registry change, and provide a verified removal command.

remediation.issue: Credential lookup traverses into shared tools and Codex configuration paths.
remediation.suggestion: Read credentials only from the proxy's dedicated configuration file with restrictive permissions. Remove ../../tools and ~/.codex token fallbacks.

content.user_title: Add Vision and Image Generation to DeepSeek
content.value_statement: Text-only DeepSeek clients cannot interpret pasted images or produce image files. This skill deploys a proxy using OCR, vision models, and generation backends.
actual_capabilities: Checks Node.js, Ollama, GPU, local ports, and Codex configuration.
Processes image data with Tesseract OCR, SiliconFlow vision, or an Ollama vision model.
Forwards Responses and Chat Completions traffic to a configurable DeepSeek upstream.
Replaces image parts with text descriptions before forwarding requests.
Calls SiliconFlow image generation and downloads returned image files.
Provides Linux, macOS, and Windows proxy startup workflows.
limitations: The proxy currently listens on all interfaces and does not authenticate clients.
Local image generation references Python backend files that are not included.
Cloud vision and generation send images or prompts to SiliconFlow.
Local vision requires Ollama, a compatible model, and sufficient memory.

use_cases.title: Enable Vision for Codex
use_cases.description: Route pasted images through OCR or a vision model before sending text to DeepSeek.
use_cases.target_user: Codex users working with text-only DeepSeek models

use_cases.title: Build a Local Vision Workflow
use_cases.description: Use Ollama and OCR to keep image analysis on the local machine.
use_cases.target_user: Privacy-focused developers with local model resources

use_cases.title: Diagnose Proxy Failures
use_cases.description: Check ports, credentials, model availability, logs, and upstream connectivity.
use_cases.target_user: Support engineers maintaining AI client integrations

prompt_templates.title: Check My Environment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my system for DeepSeek Vision Bridge. Report missing requirements and do not change files.

prompt_templates.title: Configure OCR Only
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an OCR-only setup for Codex and DeepSeek. Keep images local and request approval before editing configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Add Vision Fallbacks
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure SiliconFlow vision with Ollama fallback. Explain data destinations, credential requirements, and each proposed file change.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit and harden the bridge. Bind loopback, add client authentication, restrict outbound URLs, remove shell execution, and verify behavior.

output_examples.input: Check whether this computer can run the bridge.
output_examples.output: Node.js is available. Ollama is not running. The proxy port is free. Cloud vision needs a configured SiliconFlow key.

output_examples.input: Set up local OCR and vision without cloud services.
output_examples.output: The plan uses Tesseract and Ollama, keeps images local, and lists the configuration changes requiring approval.

output_examples.input: Why are pasted images not reaching DeepSeek correctly?
output_examples.output: The proxy is not listening on the configured port. Start it, confirm the Codex base URL, then inspect the proxy log.

best_practices: Bind the proxy to loopback and require a separate client authentication token.
Store API keys in a restricted local file and never print complete values.
Review every configuration change and test OCR, cloud vision, and fallback routes separately.
anti_patterns: Do not expose the proxy port to a local network or the public internet.
Do not pass untrusted text through shell command construction.
Do not enable cloud processing when images contain sensitive data.

faq.question: Does this make DeepSeek a native vision model?
faq.answer: No. The proxy converts images into text before sending the request to DeepSeek.

faq.question: Can image analysis remain offline?
faq.answer: Yes. Use Tesseract for text and Ollama for visual understanding without SiliconFlow.

faq.question: Which cloud service is used for vision?
faq.answer: The included configuration uses SiliconFlow with a Qwen vision model.

faq.question: Does local image generation work immediately?
faq.answer: No. The referenced Python generation backends are not included and require separate installation.

faq.question: Which API formats can the proxy process?
faq.answer: It handles OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions image content. Anthropic compatibility is documented as requiring testing.

faq.question: Is the default proxy configuration secure?
faq.answer: No. It listens on all interfaces without client authentication and requires hardening before use.
